method.summary: Frozen before any answer to the v2 scenarios or any model pick for them existed. A multinomial logit over the options of each decision (src/learn.ts). The blind model's pick is one feature; the learner adjusts from the provider's own choices, one gradient step after each answer, pulled back toward the fixed prior.
method.modelPick: The option the Azure intent model picks for the scenario, blind: no profile in the prompt (the 'none' arm of packages/agent/src/choice-eval.ts), never shown any answers. A model error gives no pick (null): the model feature is then 0 on every option.

features.model: 1 on the option the model picked
features.cat.<category>.ask: 1 on the 'ask' option, per scenario category (per-category ask tendency)
features.compromise: 1 on an option annotated as a compromise (takes a partial position between the others)
features.practical: 1 on an action option with no dimension load and no compromise flag (a fix that expresses no trade-off)
features.dim.<dimension>: the option's signed load on a profile dimension: +weight toward the right pole, -weight toward the left (horizon, risk, reputation, customer, relationships)

method.whyPrior: Set before any v2 data. With four options and every other weight 0, a model weight of 1.5 gives the model's pick a starting probability of e^1.5/(e^1.5+3) = 0.60, which matches the blind model's only measured agreement (60.5% and 63.2% on the 38 set-v1 scenarios; that aggregate is the only input). It makes the model's pick the prediction until evidence arrives, without so much confidence that a provider who consistently overrides it takes more than a few answers to be learned. Every other weight starts at 0: the profile readings did not carry over to concrete choices in set v1, so they are not used as a prior.
method.learnerNote: The learning rate and prior strength are the existing learner's defaults (src/learn.ts, src/verdicts.ts), not tuned.
method.tieRule: The option with the highest probability wins; exact ties (within 1e-12) go to the earliest option in the order a, b, c, ask.
method.order: Decisions are scored in scenario order, cs2-01 to cs2-30.

scoring.rule: Prequential accuracy: each decision is predicted from the learner's state before its answer is learned, then learned. Accuracy = correct / all 30 scenarios in the fresh set. Chance = the mean of 1/number of options. A result is only claimed when all 30 are answered.
scoring.report: Overall accuracy against the target, chance and multiple of chance, the model's pick alone for reference, and the per-category breakdown (correct / scenarios in each of the 9 categories).

method.note: The annotations describe what each option means, written with the scenarios and before any answers. They are not a guess of what the provider will choose. 'ask' options are not annotated; their features are fixed by the method.
